paragraphs: Image-to-Sphere Policy addresses how a robot can learn manipulation from a single RGB camera while benefiting from three-dimensional rotation symmetry. Earlier approaches to equivariant diffusion policies mainly used point clouds assembled from cameras fixed around the workspace. That input arrangement does not fit the increasingly common setup where the camera moves with the robot's hand.

The method projects features extracted from the camera image onto a sphere inside the diffusion policy. This representation lets the model reason about SO(3), the group describing rotations in three dimensions, without explicitly reconstructing a point cloud. Equivariance means that rotating the relevant input should produce a correspondingly transformed policy output, giving the model a structured way to handle changes in orientation.

Experiments in simulation and on real robots report consistently better performance and sample efficiency than strong baselines. The contribution is therefore both representational and practical: spherical image features bring rotation-aware policy learning to monocular RGB manipulation, extending an approach previously explored primarily with different sensing arrangements.
neurips-2025-3d-equivariant-visuomotor-p.tldr: Image-to-Sphere Policy uses spherical image features to bring rotation-equivariant robot learning to monocular RGB inputs.

paragraphs: This paper studies a mathematically tractable version of learning a flow or diffusion generative model. Its purpose is to characterize what the learned model generates and how that distribution depends on the amount of training data. The setting assumes high-dimensional data whose underlying structure lies on a lower-dimensional manifold.

The model is parameterized by a two-layer autoencoder and trained using online stochastic gradient descent. Within this specific setup, the authors derive a tight asymptotic description of low-dimensional projections of generated samples. Studying projections makes selected aspects of a complicated distribution accessible to analysis, while the explicit dependence on training-sample count connects the resulting distribution to the learning process.

The analysis also examines how mode collapse can arise: a generator can fail to represent parts of the target distribution's diversity. The authors discuss how this can lead to model collapse when generated synthetic samples become training data for another round of learning. These are possibilities established through the studied setting, rather than a claim that every diffusion model or synthetic-data training process necessarily collapses.
neurips-2025-a-solvable-model-of-learnin.tldr: A tractable generative-model analysis connects training-data quantity to generated distributions and explains how collapse can arise during synthetic-data retraining.

paragraphs: Concept bottleneck models make predictions through intermediate concepts that people can interpret. Their usefulness therefore depends on learning those concepts reliably, even when the annotations used for supervision contain mistakes. This study finds that moderate annotation corruption can damage prediction accuracy, interpretability, and the effectiveness of interventions on the concepts.

The damage is concentrated in a particularly susceptible subset of concepts. Their accuracy deteriorates much more than the average difference between clean and noisy supervision, and their corruption accounts for most of the performance loss. This finding motivates targeted protection instead of treating every concept as equally vulnerable.

The proposed framework acts during both training and inference. Sharpness-aware minimization stabilizes learning of noise-sensitive concepts during training. At inference, when clean labels are unavailable, predictive entropy ranks concepts by uncertainty so that correction focuses on the most uncertain ones. Theoretical analysis and ablations support both the robustness mechanism and uncertainty as a proxy for susceptibility. The stated result links preserving the model's interpretable intermediate representation with maintaining its predictive resilience.
neurips-2025-an-analysis-of-concept-bott.tldr: The paper identifies noise-sensitive concepts and combines robust training with uncertainty-guided correction to protect concept bottleneck models.

paragraphs: COGNAC provides cooperative reinforcement-learning environments for systems organized as networks, such as power grids, traffic signals, and computer networks. Controlling these systems involves many interacting decisions, which can make a single agent's problem difficult to scale. The benchmark supports experiments across graph sizes and connection patterns to study distributed decision-making.

Its environments connect network-control problems with practical evaluation of multi-agent learning algorithms. They support decentralized and distributed approaches, allowing researchers to examine whether methods remain effective as networks become larger and more interdependent. The tasks are designed to be simple in formulation while retaining challenging combinatorial structure.

In the reported experiments, independent actor–critic learning through IPPO produces the strongest joint policies and scales with little hyperparameter tuning. Independent value-based learning generally requires more training and is less reliable on combinatorial tasks. Centralized training and standard centralized-training/decentralized-execution methods converge more slowly, show less stability, and generalize less effectively to larger networks. The authors suggest that the latter approaches may need additional information or communication to capture network structure adequately.
neurips-2025-cognac-cooperative-graph-ba.tldr: COGNAC benchmarks cooperative network control and finds independent actor–critic learning especially effective in its tested environments.

paragraphs: Image autoregressive models generate through many sequential sampling steps, making generation slow. Distilled Decoding 2 trains a generator to produce an image in one step while learning from an existing autoregressive teacher. It addresses the quality degradation and dependence on a predefined mapping described for the earlier Distilled Decoding 1 method.

DD2 uses the teacher's conditional score in latent embedding space at each token position as its training signal. A separate network estimates the conditional score of the generated distribution. Score distillation then operates at every position, conditioned on preceding tokens. This preserves the teacher's conditional structure within the training objective while producing a generator designed for one-step sampling.

On ImageNet-256, the reported FID changes from 3.40 for the original model to 5.43 with one-step generation. Relative to DD1, DD2 reduces the stated gap between one-step and original-model performance by 67%, while achieving up to 12.3 times faster training. These results indicate a substantially improved speed–quality tradeoff, with a remaining measured difference from the original autoregressive model.
neurips-2025-distilled-decoding-2-one-st.tldr: DD2 distills autoregressive image models into one-step generators using conditional scores, reducing the reported quality gap and training cost.

paragraphs: Neural Block Linearization reduces the computational burden of running pretrained transformer language models. It replaces selected self-attention layers with linear approximations, aiming to retain useful model behavior while making inference faster. The framework can be applied without fine-tuning, so the proposed acceleration does not require another round of model training.

The approximations come from Linear Minimum Mean Squared Error estimators. To decide which layers to replace, the method uses Canonical Correlation Analysis to compute a theoretical upper bound on approximation error. Layers with the lowest estimated linearization error are selected for substitution. This gives the replacement decision an error-based criterion instead of applying the same simplification indiscriminately across the network.

Experiments report computational speed improvements with competitive accuracy across multiple reasoning benchmarks. In one example, replacing 12 self-attention layers in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B increases inference speed by 32%, with an accuracy tradeoff below 1%. The finding supports selective linearization as a practical efficiency option, while the reported example explicitly retains a small accuracy cost.
neurips-2025-efficient-large-language-mo.tldr: Neural Block Linearization speeds pretrained language models by replacing selected attention layers with error-guided linear approximations.

paragraphs: Invariant Point Attention is a geometry-aware component used in protein and RNA models. Its quadratic complexity makes longer input sequences expensive, limiting the structures that models using it can handle. FlashIPA targets this computational bottleneck so that geometry-aware modeling can extend to substantially longer sequences.

The method reformulates Invariant Point Attention through factorization and uses the hardware-efficient FlashAttention implementation. The authors report linear scaling in both GPU memory consumption and wall-clock time as sequence length increases. This matters in two distinct ways: longer inputs become more feasible to fit on a GPU, and processing them becomes less costly in elapsed computation time.

FlashIPA matches or exceeds standard IPA performance while reducing computational costs in the reported evaluation. The authors also retrain generative models without length restrictions and generate structures containing thousands of residues. That demonstration connects the computational reformulation to a modeling capability: the efficiency improvement enables training at lengths that were previously unattainable in their setup.
neurips-2025-flash-invariant-point-atten.tldr: FlashIPA reformulates geometry-aware attention to reduce computation and enable generative modeling of structures with thousands of residues.

paragraphs: GauDP addresses a perception problem in collaborative robotics: each agent needs detailed information for its own actions while also understanding the shared environment. Methods that handle these needs poorly can produce weak coordination and become harder to scale as more agents participate. The paper proposes a shared representation for perception-aware imitation learning.

Starting from RGB images captured from local viewpoints, GauDP reconstructs a globally consistent three-dimensional Gaussian field. Every agent can dynamically query this common scene representation for features relevant to its task. The design connects individual visual observations to shared spatial information, supporting both local control and coordinated behavior without adding another sensing modality.

Evaluation on RoboFactory covers diverse manipulation tasks involving multiple robot arms. GauDP outperforms existing image-based methods and approaches the effectiveness of methods driven by point clouds. The authors also report strong scalability as agent count increases, with ablations and visualizations supporting robustness and efficiency. The findings suggest that shared three-dimensional structure recovered from images can improve collaboration while retaining RGB-based sensing.
neurips-2025-gaudp-reinventing-multi-age.tldr: GauDP builds a shared 3D Gaussian scene from local RGB views to improve coordination among collaborating robots.

paragraphs: Latent reasoning uses internal hidden states to carry computation between reasoning steps. This offers richer continuous information than a single sampled sequence of words, but it can conflict with the discrete token generation used by language models. The paper develops a hybrid approach that retains token generation while incorporating internal features.

Hybrid reasoning policy optimization, or HRPO, uses a learnable gate to combine previous hidden states with sampled tokens. Training begins mainly with token embeddings and gradually incorporates more hidden features. Token sampling also introduces the stochasticity needed for reinforcement-learning optimization, allowing the method to train without requiring chain-of-thought trajectories as supervision.

Evaluations across diverse benchmarks report improvements over prior methods on both knowledge-intensive and reasoning-intensive tasks. The authors also report that the resulting models remain interpretable and exhibit cross-lingual patterns and shorter completions. Together, these findings support combining continuous internal computation with discrete generation as a way to develop reasoning through reinforcement learning while preserving the language model's generative capabilities.
neurips-2025-hybrid-latent-reasoning-via.tldr: HRPO combines hidden-state computation with sampled tokens to train hybrid reasoning through reinforcement learning without chain-of-thought supervision.

paragraphs: IRRISIGHT addresses the shortage of detailed, large-scale data for studying agricultural water availability. Water conditions depend on natural factors and human activity, so satellite images alone need not capture all relevant information. Combining sources is difficult because geographic alignment, data formats, labels, and class frequencies can differ.

The dataset contains 1.4 million aligned image patches, each 224 by 224 pixels, spanning 20 U.S. states. Its processing pipeline brings raster, vector, and point data onto a shared 10-meter grid and combines satellite imagery with environmental attributes. Structured prompts informed by domain knowledge also turn tabular attributes into natural-language descriptions, supporting models that process both images and text.

The authors use irrigation-type classification as a representative task and benchmark vision and vision–language models. Training and test regions are spatially separate, making geographic separation part of the evaluation design. The results show substantial performance improvements from multimodal representations. The contribution combines a reusable data resource with a scalable alignment pipeline, creating a foundation for further machine-learning research on water availability.
neurips-2025-irrisight-a-large-scale-mul.tldr: IRRISIGHT combines satellite imagery and environmental data at scale, with irrigation benchmarks showing benefits from multimodal inputs.

paragraphs: This paper studies classification when obtaining additional information has a cost. A first classifier sees features x and can either predict immediately or pay to consult a second classifier that sees both x and additional features z. Both classifiers are trained jointly, making the decision to defer part of the overall learning problem.

The desired objective charges for incorrect predictions and adds a penalty c whenever the second stage is consulted. This captures the practical tradeoff between making a cheaper decision and acquiring more informative features. However, the resulting classification-and-cost loss is difficult to use directly for training, motivating a more manageable substitute.

The main contribution is a hinge-based surrogate loss with a consistency guarantee: consistency for the surrogate implies consistency for the original cost-sensitive objective. This connects an easier training target to the decision problem the system is meant to solve. The result is a theoretical justification for the substitute objective, rather than a claim that any finite training run will automatically find the best acquisition policy.
neurips-2025-is-the-acquisition-worth-th.tldr: The paper derives a trainable surrogate with a consistency guarantee for jointly learning when to classify and when to purchase additional features.

paragraphs: Three-dimensional semantic scene completion estimates both scene geometry and the meanings of its parts for autonomous-driving perception. FlowScene addresses the difficulty of using information across time. A single frame provides sparse evidence, while simply stacking features from several frames can overlook motion and produce temporally inconsistent representations.

The method uses optical flow to guide how observations across frames are combined. Its temporal aggregation module aligns and merges features to capture motion-aware context and deformable structures. A second module brings occlusion masks and the aggregated features into three-dimensional voxel space, where it adaptively refines the representation used for geometric modeling.

These components give motion and visibility explicit roles in scene completion, helping the model use changing viewpoints and contextual evidence rather than treating successive frames as interchangeable inputs. The authors report state-of-the-art results, with mean intersection-over-union scores of 17.70 on SemanticKITTI and 20.81 on SSCBench-KITTI-360. The stated findings support optical-flow-guided temporal integration as an effective approach to improving scene-completion accuracy on those benchmarks.
neurips-2025-learning-temporal-3d-semant.tldr: FlowScene uses optical flow and occlusion information to combine video evidence into more accurate 3D semantic scene completion.

paragraphs: This paper studies a relaxed form of coupling probability distributions. One distribution supplies a list of samples, and a match succeeds if any list entry equals the sample drawn from the other distribution. Allowing several candidates changes the matching problem and creates opportunities in both language generation and compression.

The authors extend Gumbel-max sampling to this setting and derive a lower bound on the probability of acceptance, called the list matching lemma. They use the construction for multi-draft speculative sampling, where several draft candidates can contribute to token generation. The resulting mechanism is simple to implement, performs competitively with SpecTr and SpecInfer across language tasks, and provides both a token-acceptance bound and a qualified guarantee of drafter invariance.

A second application compresses a source sample for multiple decoders, each possessing independent side information. A compression method based on the same sampling generalization yields significant experimental gains on synthetic Gaussian sources and MNIST images. The contribution connects one probabilistic matching construction to two distinct computational uses.
neurips-2025-list-level-distribution-cou.tldr: A list-based distribution-coupling method supplies acceptance guarantees and practical applications in speculative decoding and distributed lossy compression.

paragraphs: MonoLift aims to give a robot useful three-dimensional understanding while using only a single RGB camera at deployment. Such images are convenient to acquire but lack explicit structural information, which can hurt action estimation. Extra 3D sensors add acquisition overhead, while running a pretrained depth estimator can add substantial inference cost.

The method transfers knowledge from a depth-guided teacher to an RGB-only student during training. Distillation happens at three levels: spatial features that represent geometry, temporal dynamics that describe behavior over time, and action-level policy behavior. Supervising all three is intended to teach the student both how the scene is structured and how that structure should inform control.

Experiments on simulated and real-world manipulation tasks show improvements over existing monocular approaches. MonoLift also surpasses several methods that use explicit 3D inputs. These findings support moving depth-guided learning into training so the deployed student can perform geometry-aware control from RGB alone, combining the stated performance benefits with a lighter sensing and inference setup.
neurips-2025-monolift-learning-3d-manipu.tldr: MonoLift distills geometry, temporal behavior, and actions from a depth-guided teacher into an RGB-only robot policy.

paragraphs: Medical-image harmonization reduces appearance differences caused by scanners so images can be compared more consistently. Paired images from different devices are difficult to rely on in practice, but methods using unpaired images can alter anatomy. This paper addresses that preservation problem for optical coherence tomography images.

The authors examine Schrödinger bridges, which match image distributions through entropy-regularized optimal transport. They identify the squared Euclidean image distance used as transport cost as a source of anatomical changes: images depicting the same anatomy can still be far apart under this measure. Consequently, similarity in raw image space does not adequately represent the similarity that harmonization should preserve.

The proposed latent metric Schrödinger bridge uses an invertible network to map images into a learned space where distances between images with the same anatomy are minimized through a pullback metric. Distribution matching then occurs in that space. The authors report superiority over directly applying a Schrödinger bridge to OCT harmonization, supporting anatomy-guided distance design as a way to improve anatomical consistency.
neurips-2025-optical-coherence-tomograph.tldr: An anatomy-guided latent distance improves Schrödinger-bridge harmonization of OCT images across scanner appearances.

paragraphs: Reason-RFT develops visual reasoning through a combination of supervised training and reinforcement learning. The paper identifies a possible weakness of relying on annotated chain-of-thought examples alone: models may overfit those reasoning patterns and adapt poorly when the data domain changes. Its framework is designed to improve flexibility after that initial supervision.

The first stage uses curated reasoning traces for supervised fine-tuning to activate the model's reasoning capabilities. The second applies Group Relative Policy Optimization, generating multiple reasoning-and-response pairs to improve adaptability. For evaluation, the authors reconstruct a dataset covering visual counting, structural perception, and spatial transformation, providing three distinct dimensions of visual reasoning.

The reported experiments show state-of-the-art performance and improvements over both open-source and proprietary models in the evaluation. Reason-RFT also maintains robust performance under domain shifts and performs strongly with few examples, surpassing supervised fine-tuning baselines trained on full datasets. These findings support reinforcement fine-tuning as a useful extension of supervised reasoning training, particularly for generalization and data efficiency.
neurips-2025-reason-rft-reinforcement-fi.tldr: Reason-RFT follows supervised reasoning training with reinforcement learning to improve visual reasoning, domain-shift robustness, and few-shot performance.

paragraphs: Detecting defects in three-dimensional point clouds requires distinguishing structural irregularities from changes in how an object is oriented. The paper argues that existing memory-bank methods can struggle with inconsistent feature transformations and insufficient sensitivity to local geometry. Failed registration, the alignment of point clouds, can make detection particularly unreliable.

The proposed framework uses registration as part of learning the features used for anomaly detection. Registration and memory-based detection both depend on local geometric structure and feature similarity across samples, so their objectives are integrated. Jointly learning alignment and representation encourages features that retain useful local distinctions while remaining robust to rotation.

This changes the role of registration from an alignment operation into a source of guidance for the detector's representation. Experiments on Anomaly-ShapeNet and Real3D-AD report consistent improvements over existing approaches in effectiveness and generalizability. The findings support training features around the shared geometric demands of registration and defect detection, rather than relying only on alignment to make comparisons reliable.
neurips-2025-registration-is-a-powerful-.tldr: Jointly learning point-cloud registration and anomaly features improves rotation robustness and 3D defect detection in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Continually trained language models must learn new tasks while preserving earlier knowledge. Replaying old examples can help, but those examples may no longer be accessible. SERS develops pseudo-rehearsal, using synthesized training material, to address problems with task relevance, unstable generated outputs, and neglect of relationships between tasks.

The framework separates prompt creation from label creation. Semantic masking and template guidance produce varied, task-relevant prompts without an additional generation module. For labels, it blends the base model's prior knowledge with outputs from the fine-tuned model, aiming to prevent excessive specialization. A dynamic regularizer then adjusts constraints according to task similarity, measured using Wasserstein distance between task distributions.

These components address different parts of the stability–plasticity tradeoff: what examples to rehearse, what responses to learn from, and how strongly to constrain learning. Across diverse tasks and different language models, SERS reduces forgetting by more than two percentage points relative to strong pseudo-rehearsal baselines. The reported result supports combining task-aware synthetic rehearsal with adaptive constraints to preserve knowledge during continued learning.
neurips-2025-self-evolving-pseudo-rehear.tldr: SERS reduces language-model forgetting through task-relevant synthetic rehearsal, evolving labels, and similarity-dependent regularization.

paragraphs: SHGR is a dependence measure intended to capture relationships that ordinary correlation coefficients can miss, especially nonlinear relationships and dependencies involving multiple variables. It draws inspiration from HGR maximal correlation, which searches for nonlinear transformations that make two variables as strongly Pearson-correlated as possible. Optimizing over such transformations makes HGR difficult to estimate.

The proposed coefficient instead builds on Spearman rank correlation. The authors develop neural-network estimators for three settings: a matrix of pairwise correlations, relationships between a group of variables and another variable, and relationships between two groups of variables. Tailored network architectures are used to keep computation competitive across these different estimation problems.

The paper states that SHGR satisfies Rényi's axioms and detects nonlinear dependencies while showing robustness to noise, outliers, and spurious correlations. Numerical experiments and feature-selection tasks report performance above existing state-of-the-art methods. The contribution combines a generalized correlation definition with practical estimators, linking the mathematical properties of the measure to empirical usefulness in identifying informative relationships.
neurips-2025-shgr-a-generalized-maximal-.tldr: SHGR combines rank-based maximal correlation with neural estimators to detect nonlinear and multivariate dependencies.

paragraphs: Preference-based reinforcement learning learns rewards from human comparisons instead of requiring a hand-designed reward function. In tasks with several stages, however, comparisons can be uninformative when they involve different kinds of activity. Comparing navigation against grasping, for example, may provide less useful guidance about how either stage should be performed.

STAIR addresses this stage-misalignment problem by learning approximate stages and prioritizing comparisons within them. It learns temporal distance through contrastive learning, grouping states that are close in time into coherent stages. The stage representation requires no predefined task knowledge and adapts as the policy changes, allowing comparison selection to follow the agent's evolving behavior.

The authors support the underlying problem with theoretical analysis and empirical experiments. STAIR performs better in multi-stage tasks while remaining competitive in single-stage tasks. Human studies also find that its approximated stages agree with human cognition. Together, these results support organizing preference queries around comparable portions of behavior as a way to make feedback more informative for reward learning.
neurips-2025-stair-addressing-stage-misa.tldr: STAIR improves preference-based learning by identifying task stages and prioritizing comparisons between behavior segments from the same stage.

paragraphs: Ensemble learning is commonly explained as a way to reduce variance by combining several models. This paper studies a different benefit: reducing the probability of unusually poor generalization. Its focus is the tail of excess risk, which describes how likely a learned model is to perform substantially worse than the relevant risk reference.

The proposed procedure repeatedly applies a base learner to subsamples and selects the model that appears most frequently. For base learners with reasonable predictive ability, the authors show that this can produce exponentially decaying excess-risk tails even when the original learner has only polynomial decay. The qualification about the starting learner matters: the result does not assert that ensembling supplies predictive ability from an arbitrary ineffective learner.

An improvement in the decay rate goes beyond merely lowering a variance value; it changes how sharply the probability of poor outcomes diminishes. Numerical examples involving heavy-tailed data or intrinsically slow rates show substantial improvements in out-of-sample performance. The paper thus offers a reliability-oriented explanation for why subsampled ensembles can help.
neurips-2025-subsampled-ensemble-can-imp.tldr: Selecting the most frequent model across subsamples can improve excess-risk tails from polynomial to exponential decay for suitably predictive base learners.

paragraphs: TF-MAS searches for effective Mamba2 architectures without training candidate networks as part of the search. Training-based architecture search can require substantial computation because assessing alternatives involves learning their parameters. The paper develops a proxy tailored to Mamba2 so candidates can be ranked through a cheaper architectural evaluation.

The proxy is motivated by rank collapse in stacked State Space Duality blocks. It requires computing a transformation matrix and its gradient between two tensors within the network. The authors also define a corresponding architecture search space and propose a method for choosing the ranges of adjustable hyperparameters, making the proxy part of a complete search procedure.

Experiments report better ranking correlation and better resulting architectures than all existing training-free search approaches evaluated for Mamba2. Ranking correlation concerns how effectively the proxy orders candidates, while search-result performance concerns the quality of the architectures ultimately selected. Improvements in both support the value of using a Mamba2-specific signal. The authors describe TF-MAS as, to their knowledge, the first training-free search method designed for Mamba-type networks.
neurips-2025-tf-mas-training-free-mamba2.tldr: TF-MAS uses a rank-collapse-inspired proxy to search Mamba2 architectures without training candidates during search.

paragraphs: This paper improves the ability of unified vision–language models to produce sequences that alternate between text and images. Such interleaving matters for visual storytelling and step-by-step visual reasoning, where each element must fit the surrounding sequence. The approach adapts existing models without depending on large-scale datasets of interleaved outputs.

Training begins with a warm-up dataset mixing curated interleaved sequences with limited multimodal-understanding and text-to-image examples. This introduces the desired output patterns while preserving pretrained capabilities. The next stage extends Group Relative Policy Optimization to handle text and image generation together within one decoding trajectory.

Hybrid rewards evaluate textual relevance, alignment between images and text, and structural fidelity. Additional process-level rewards provide guidance at individual steps, helping training on complex multimodal tasks. Experiments on MMIE and InterleavedBench report significant gains in output quality and coherence. The stated findings support optimizing the mixed sequence as a connected generation process, with feedback on both its individual parts and their relationships.
neurips-2025-towards-unified-multimodal-.tldr: A multimodal extension of GRPO improves coherent interleaved text-and-image generation using hybrid and step-level rewards.

paragraphs: Long-tailed recognition involves classes with very different amounts of training data. Improving rare tail classes while retaining strong performance on common head classes is difficult, and directly combining several training strategies through multi-objective optimization can be unstable. TS-MOF separates representation learning from classifier adaptation to make that combination more manageable.

After standard pretraining, the framework freezes the feature backbone and fine-tunes specialized classifier heads using multiple objectives. One component adjusts task weights according to current per-class performance. Another resolves conflicts between gradients and combines them constructively. Together, these mechanisms address both how much emphasis each objective receives and how competing update directions are reconciled.

Experiments on CIFAR100-LT, ImageNet-LT, and iNaturalist 2018 report state-of-the-art results with improvements across head and tail classes. The abstract highlights a 3.3% tail-accuracy improvement on CIFAR100-LT at imbalance ratio 100, alongside better head performance, using 20 fine-tuning epochs. The findings support focused classifier adaptation as an efficient way to combine long-tailed recognition strategies without retraining the feature backbone.
neurips-2025-ts-mof-two-stage-multi-obje.tldr: TS-MOF freezes pretrained features and coordinates classifier objectives to improve both common and rare class recognition.

paragraphs: WISA addresses the difficulty text-to-video models have in generating motion and events that obey physical laws. The paper attributes this partly to a gap between abstract physical concepts and the guidance available to generative models. It introduces both a framework for representing physical knowledge and a dataset with explicit physical content.

The framework organizes physical knowledge into textual descriptions, qualitative categories, and quantitative properties. Modules including Mixture-of-Physical-Experts Attention and a Physical Classifier encode these attributes to guide generation. This decomposition gives the model several forms of physical information, connecting verbal descriptions with categorical and numerical representations of the same underlying principles.

WISA-80K contains 80,000 human-curated videos depicting 17 fundamental laws across dynamics, thermodynamics, and optics. It addresses the weak or implicit representation of physics in many existing video datasets. Experiments with models including CogVideoX and Wan2.1 report substantially improved physical alignment and notable gains on VideoPhy. These findings demonstrate better adherence in the evaluated setting, rather than a guarantee that generated videos always satisfy physical laws.
neurips-2025-wisa-world-simulator-assist.tldr: WISA combines structured physical guidance with a curated physics-video dataset to improve physical consistency in text-to-video generation.
